I think I need to preface this, I'm not really sure why I want to share this, but I really want to.

Also, if you looked at my record, you'd think I was a really gung-ho Soldier. On active duty, I was a Combat Engineer, did 12 months of combat patrols in Baghdad(mostly as a gunner on a HMMWV), and 15 months of route clearance all over Iraq. I got a Combat Action Badge for a firefight on my first patrol in Baghdad, I as awarded a Bronze Star Medal as a Specialist/E4(for non-military, it's almost unheard of for E6 or below to get one, it shouldn't be, but that's how it works), Purple Heart recipient, and enough ARCOMs that I'm tired of getting them.

Now for the real me: tall, goofy, nerdy white guy. Super shy, kind of awkward. Easily distracted, but focused when I need to be, and constantly making jokes and causing mischief.

And here's the story: Middle of the summer in 2006 in Baghdad, our task force is working with Iraqi Army to cordon off a neighborhood (al-Asariyah, I think) and search every house. I'm with 5 Iraqis going door to door and searching for contraband. We get to a house with a locked door, and I'm super excited. This is my chance, I finally get to kick down a door! I stop the Iraqi that was about to kick it down, get some space, and Boom! :-( I kicked too low. The bottom half came off the hinge, the Iraqis crouch down and go through, clearing the room, and I follow, feeling disappointment. As I'm standing back up, the bottom half of the door slides out from underneath me, I land flat on my back, the Iraqis laugh and give me a hand up. Probably the most embarrassing thing that has ever happened.
Ohhh...but thank you for your service. You're one of the great ones. Klutzy or not.
Lol, thank you. I always feel awkward when people thank me for my service.

Ok, I laughed. But seriously, doesn't matter what you look like if you have the guts to put on the uniform and go out and do a job like that. I'd think that those Iraqis you were patrolling with were plenty happy to have you there, and I'm glad that there was someone willing to step up and do the job for our country. You got my respect, bud.
:-D thank you. I actually laugh about it now, too.
